D002_m001.question:
It’s been about a year, maybe a bit more, that this has really started to mess with my life, but when I look back, I was kind of like this even in elementary school—teachers always said I was “bright but careless.”

Now in grad school it’s become impossible to ignore. I keep making these stupid little mistakes on assignments and in the lab—like skipping a step in a protocol or misreading numbers—even when I understand the material. I’ll read an article and realize I’ve zoned out and have no idea what I just read, so I reread it three times and still miss key points.

When professors give multi-step instructions, I start with good intentions but somehow drift off halfway through and end up turning things in half-finished or late. My apartment is the same: I’ll start doing dishes, then wander off to answer an email, then find myself scrolling on my phone, and the sink is still full.

My mind is constantly jumping—to random worries, ideas, things I need to Google. I get pulled away by every little noise or thought. Physically I’m not bouncing around, but inside I feel restless, like I can’t settle into anything for more than a few minutes.
D002_m001.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D002_m002.question:
Well, I’ve always been a bit “scattered,” even as a boy in school – teachers used to say I daydreamed and missed things on the board – but over the last year or so it’s become much more of a problem. My wife says it’s been about a year and a month since she really started noticing it.

These days I misread things all the time. I’ll pay a bill and overlook a line, or fill out a form and leave whole sections blank without realizing it. When my wife asks me to do a few simple things around the house—take out the rubbish, ring the plumber, pick something up—I’ll start, then drift off, and half of it never gets done. I’ll go into a room and genuinely have no idea what I went in for.

I find my mind wandering constantly. I can be watching the news and suddenly I’m off thinking about something from years ago, and I’ve missed the whole report. Even conversations are hard to follow if there’s any noise around. I don’t run about, obviously, but I do feel oddly “keyed up,” like I can’t settle, shifting in my chair, getting up and down a lot, as if I’m internally restless.
D002_m002.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
